# fereg 0.5.0 beta status

**Last updated:** 2026-09-26
**Branch:** main
**Mode:** prototype/development
**Release state:** public OLS and PPML beta surfaces; no qualified release,
tag, or Windows scientific qualification.

This is the sole mutable progress/handover record. Historical receipts remain
unchanged under benchmarks/reports/. This opening supersedes previous next-step
directions. The multi-FE PPML <=0.90-times-comparable-stock goal remains active.
**The one-pass incidence experiment is closed and rejected.** Production remains
exactly **residualrows2**, accepted at **ceb8f53d**, with all 567 computational
inputs matching. The next boundary is a single-use current-frame response-statistic
handoff, with explicit proof of units, rounding and independent acceptance.
Fresh seed **202609447** is consumed; do not tune on it or reuse earlier frozen
validation seeds. No candidate or task-owned job is pending.

### Next implementation: single-use canonical response statistics

Do not reopen incidence tuning or spend a cycle on 5-ms immutable topology setup.
Paired diagnostics leave **16 ms** in canonical norm scans and **20 ms** in
`finalize_reported_bread_and_intercept`; its containing assembly also has **14 ms**
of independent finite score checks. These are disjoint subspans, not license to
remove the checks or assume the entire containing cost is avoidable.

Inspect `Products.means[0]`, `Products.norms[0]`, `CanonicalMoments`,
`try_canonical_products`, `solve_full_retained_rank` and
`finalize_reported_bread_and_intercept`. Canonical products compute current-response
statistics but transfer only control statistics and the finite Gram; the rank
owner rescans response norms and the intercept identity obtains the outcome mean
again. Investigate carrying certified statistics with the already single-use
moment handoff, preserving the fresh raw-residual-mean identity and score checks.
Prove normalized-weight units, actual reconstructed-row rounding, zero/underflow,
rank sensitivity and changing-frame/rollback ownership. A scaled Gram diagonal is
not automatically equivalent to the stable residual norm. No stale weight or
response authority may cross generations. Validate against independent weighted
and Poisson/Hessian oracles before measuring new frozen/fresh cases.

This materially different canonical boundary can help fast and low construction;
keep categorical/absorbed-slope and shared OLS controls. The broader multi-FE
speed goal remains active and unproven.

## Further PPML development plan — after canonical construction, 2026-09-25

Scope remains **at least two FE**. Aim for complete public `feppml` time
**<=0.90 times scientifically comparable pinned stock per case**, preferably
0.80–0.85 for headroom. Computational organization may be replaced substantially;
scientific accuracy, samples, rank, weights, inference and publication may not.
Current computation is **canonicalthree1 / ADR 0210**, with 566 matching inputs.
The source-bound report linked in the opening supplies current distributions.
Do not pool clocks across source artifacts or transfer historical wins.

|Fresh two-FE factors N153600/K19/T8|418/508 ms; all 0.794–0.837|Protect accepted finite-block advantage|

Seed347 remains for development. Seeds through **202609440** are consumed/frozen;
**441 is unconsumed**. Default fixest accuracy failures remain separate. The
original five-to-eightfold slope timings belong to older artifacts; current
simple slopes are70/80 ms while four slopes 120/119 do not meet the objective.

### Completed bounded milestones

1. **Finite conditioning:** full current-weight finite Gram retained (ADR 0208).
   Borrowed representatives and blanket ordinary-engine replacement rejected
   (ADRs 0209/0207); do not resume selected-view tuning or accumulate layers.
2. **Three-FE canonical construction:** full response/control geometry, independent
   products/certificates and one retained write adopted (ADR 0210). Hard fast/low
   factor gains 15–26% development,15–18% fresh; low numeric 31%. Initial/strict
   low-factor diagnostic construction 179/175->82/89 ms. This closes that slice,
   not the large-N two-FE budget. OLS exports are exact; the known baseline
   report-flag assertion remains open and documented.

### Next milestone: large-N two-FE ownership and construction

Use the already captured exclusive trace rather than rerunning an inventory.
The current dense two-FE product route declines at levels 163840/4096 and N983040.
Initial and strict canonical construction each cost roughly 250 ms. Initial
materialization ~45, means ~23, own norms ~18, borrowed norms ~28, certificate ~30,
finite rank ~37 ms; strict raw statistics ~46, norms ~37 combined, transport ~12,
certificate ~20, finite rank ~47 ms. Production preparation ~230 and publication ~122
also matter. These are specific measured opportunities, not additive proof that
all their scientific work can disappear. Ordinary directions alone cannot
supply 460 ms.

Implement a coherent **implicit two-FE full-frame construction and cross-stage
ownership** design where dense reduced geometry is unaffordable. Reuse the
existing implicit Schur/operator machinery with once-per-current-frame preparation,
independent RHS stopping, original-input acceptance, certified finite products
and one retained-row owner. Compare this organization against retaining the
projector while eliminating proven repeated normalization/means/materialization
scans; at most two materially different candidates. Do not resume isolated
Schur matvec, incidence, frame-cache or panel-size probes. A new design must
change total construction and handoff cost, including low-memory scratch traffic.

Build a nonoverlapping byte/pass ledger from SPI loading through preparation,
initialization, initial rank, ordinary solves, score/objective, strict/final
Hessian, inference and publication. Track each observation-sized owner, consumer,
copy and generation. Native inclusive phase timers cannot be added to their
children. Transfer compatible owners and fuse same-frame reductions without
sharing solver acceptance authority. Keep immutable originals and minimal
current-weight state. Bound scratch/worker work without silently adding N-by-K
storage. Measure several N/K values to distinguish fixed setup from throughput.

Required acceptance checks may be implemented more efficiently when equivalence
is explicit and tested. Cheap iterative diagnostics can guide proposals; fresh
original-input residual, model-space, rank, finite-solve, score, objective,
reconstruction and exact final q*mu Hessian remain. Prior solutions are guesses
under new weights. Preserve strict rollback and physical response anchors.
Retain Stata control/Rust computation, main-thread SPI and receipt-last atomicity.

Target a material portion of the 460/246-ms deficits, not another isolated
few-millisecond win. After each implementation, identify residual costs once;
if canonical construction cannot close the gap, cross the next measured
preparation/publication ownership boundary rather than retuning the same kernel.

### Carryover and scientific coverage

Protect three-FE factor/numeric, two-FE generated, serial/narrow, wide,
disconnected, low-memory, slopes and four-plus FE through focused controls.
Keep robust/cluster inference, means/all outputs, T1/T4/T8, memory refusal and
OLS control exports. Address small-three-FE and four-slope losses with broad
preparation/certificate/inference/output gains where the measured budget supports
it. The old residual-space extrapolation and serial weighted-OLS rounds remain
closed. No guard may depend on benchmark names or favorable seeds.

Extend adaptively to weak connectivity, zeros, offsets/separation, prior weights,
several slopes and rank deficiency. Establish comparable sample, objective,
separation, DoF/VCE and output work before ranking stock. Use independent explicit
Poisson/Hessian/sandwich and weighted-design oracles; ordinary fixest weights
cannot establish Stata frequency-weight inference. Small full-output success
does not adjudicate older large full-output discrepancies. Keep static allocation
drift, weighted constrained fits and nonretaining CG open. No SCC authentication
retry; Linux T1/8/16 and physical-cap evidence await renewed access.

### Acceptance and stopping rules

Each bounded milestone: pinned baseline science/timing, dominant avoidable cost,
smallest coherent implementation, focused independent/boundary checks, three
B/C/stock rotations, frozen candidate and five predeclared fresh rotations,
then commit or reject with distributions and failure evidence. Seek 20–40% family
improvements where the budget supports them; retain inexpensive reliable smaller
carryover gains. All paired fresh ratios must support a robust 0.90 claim. A noisy
boundary gets one confirmation block, not endless threshold tuning.

Keep stock unmodified at `glm.tol=1e-10`, `fixef.tol=1e-11`, matched threads and
work. Diagnostic instrumentation is separate. No compilation, audit, profile,
archive or competing fits alongside headline clocks. Preserve monitor failures,
application errors/timeouts and scientific discrepancies. Bind exact source and
artifact identities; frozen 77/16/111 stay unchanged. STATUS is the only mutable
handover, ADRs contain decisions and reports immutable evidence. Finish coherent
milestones as clean local commits. No push/release, plugins, full qualification or
stopped-campaign restart. The broad performance objective remains unfinished.

### Next implementation plan: close the remaining public-command gaps

Optimize **each comparable family toward <=0.90 stock**, with distributions and
losses, not an aggregate win count. On these fresh inputs, threaded two-slope
PPML must fall **94 to <=72 ms** (23.4% of current time); narrow categorical must
fall **42 to <=26.1 ms** (37.9%). These require broader work than a matrix-kernel
adjustment. Continue protecting the eight winning cases rather than retuning on
their validation seeds. The accepted solver already has coefficient Schur CG,
current-weight QR/coupling, independent column stopping, joint warm directions,
profiled starts/trials and canonical-first finalization; do not propose these as
new mechanisms or reopen their rejected variants without materially new evidence.

1. **Make canonical frame construction one coherent pipeline.** The norm
   handoff is the first completed piece. Next bind original/generated columns,
   normalized weights, reference statistics and retained rows once per valid
   frame. Fuse remaining means/scales and product visits with necessary loading
   or reconstruction, and remove copies whose ownership can transfer. Preserve
   explicit projected-column rank and exact final-Hessian authority. Test a
   fresh certificate on a finite residual already assembled from certified
   columns, invoking corrective projection only on refusal. This retains an
   independent check and targets avoidable solving, rather than adding full
   checks around speculative updates. Current diagnostic rank-residual work is
   about **2.6 ms** on two slopes and **5.9/6.4 ms** on large fast/low cases;
   this is an upper budget, not a promised saving. Measure complete canonical
   construction and public calls, including refusal and low-memory behavior.

2. **Use a real canonical Newton checkpoint as the second convergence witness.**
   Investigate scheduling it after the first accepted convergence pass so that
   its independently checked result can supply the second objective/score
   predicate and final-Hessian products. Preserve both convergence predicates,
   actual Newton movement, all strict comparisons and recovery after refusal.
   Retained products must still match the final accepted q*mu frame exactly.
   The target is elimination of a complete redundant ordinary solve and its
   frame refresh, not the rejected zero-Newton shortcut. Write a successor ADR
   and independent truth/rank-loss/extreme-weight/rejection/rollback tests before
   adoption. If this cannot establish equivalent scientific authority, reject it
   rather than weaken the contract or extend speculative fallback layers.

3. **Build a smaller end-to-end execution path for narrow categorical PPML.**
   Its remaining gap is larger than its entire ~7.7-ms diagnostic canonical
   construction cost, so canonical-only tuning cannot suffice. Measure the
   whole public command's loading, topology/start, ordinary iterations, accepted
   score/objective passes, inference and publication at the current narrow input.
   Consolidate shared immutable sample/topology ownership and compatible current-
   frame observation passes across these stages. Reuse the existing joint and
   canonical engines where efficient; replace duplicated owners or traversals
   when the complete cost supports it. Use observed mathematical dimensions/work
   for dispatch, never seeds or benchmark names. Keep isolated ADO metadata
   tuning, full Schur-factor and paired-lane experiments closed. A bounded pilot
   must identify enough removable work to address the ~16-ms gap before a larger
   redesign or fresh campaign is warranted.

4. **Broaden beyond positive numeric robust-plus-mu fits.** Run a small current-
   source screen of supported weights, generated/factor terms, clustered
   inference, additional requested outputs and wider controls. Classify samples,
   separation and inference comparability before ranking stock times. Use
   independent explicit-design WLS/Poisson/Hessian oracles for scientific gaps;
   ordinary fixest weights remain unsuitable as a Stata frequency-weight oracle.
   Prioritize the largest measured shared cost, not every conceivable option.
   Carry successful mechanisms to multipartition OLS only with separate evidence.

5. **Accept in bounded, committed milestones.** Each candidate gets a frozen-
   frame operation comparison, independent boundary oracles, small alternating
   B/C/stock pilot and, only if promising, predeclared fresh controls. Match threads,
   outputs and work; keep diagnostic reference builds separate from stock. Include
   T1/T4/T8, fast/low, imbalance, weak/disconnected topology, multiple slopes,
   rank deficiency and changing weights without a Cartesian campaign. Prefer
   >=10% whole-command gains; keep smaller shared changes only when repeatable

   threshold tuning. Report remaining time budgets, failures and memory costs,
   remove superseded code and commit accepted improvements. Linux T1/8/16 and
   physical-memory confirmation remain deferred until access is renewed.

## Renewed plan: a 10% public PPML advantage — 2026-09-25

The target is **complete public PPML time <=0.90 times scientifically comparable
pinned stock fixest, for designs with at least two FE**. Evaluate it by family,
including inference and requested outputs, rather than by an aggregate win rate.
This planning update adopts no numerical change. The accepted runtime remains
`frameado3` at **132b69b6**, with the shared-factor closeout at **6a1eb064**.
The three modified Rust files contain an unfinished geometry/preparation
experiment; preserve them and their evidence until its explicit adopt/reject
decision. Earlier next-step lists below are historical.

### Current savings budgets

Use the final fresh415 block in the
[accepted-source report](benchmarks/reports/development/ppml-command-framing-local-2026-09-25/README.md).
These are warm public-command medians on the local Mac, not cold-start or
cross-platform claims. The unpublished current experiment has no ranked timing.

| Family | N/K/T; mode | Accepted / stock ms | 0.90-stock target | Further saving needed |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Two slope partitions |38400/6/8; fast|126 / 89|80.1|45.9 ms / 36.4%|
| Two categorical FE |26880/2/4; fast|44 / 34|30.6|13.4 ms / 30.5%|
| Disconnected categorical |48000/12/8; fast|100 / 89|80.1|19.9 ms / 19.9%|
| Three FE slopes, unbalanced |72960/10/8; low|282 / 279|251.1|30.9 ms / 11.0%|
| Three FE slopes, unbalanced |72960/10/8; fast|260 / 281|252.9|7.1 ms / 2.7%|
| Two categorical FE, serial |25920/3/1; fast|67 / 65|58.5|8.5 ms / 12.7%|
| Four categorical FE |32160/10/4; low|231 / 558|502.2|Already clears target|

### Evidence that changes the next implementation

The isolated `jointphases1` diagnostic, based on 6a1eb064, profiles actual
ordinary joint calls at their scheduled tolerances. Receipts, build identity,
profile recipe and audit are under `target/ppml-joint-moments-20260925`.
The two diagnostic rotations have **20 passing public states and 10 exact
baseline scientific comparisons**. No diagnostic clock is a stock ranking.

For the existing large N61440/K10/T8 tuning case, ordinary joint FE products
cost about **18 ms**, weighted geometry **10 ms** and pair preparation **6 ms**;
projected columns plus their finite Hessian cost about **6 ms**. The small
two-partition N30720/K6/T8 case instead spends about **11 ms** on geometry and
**7 ms** on coupling, but only **1.4 ms** on FE products. These distinct designs
must not be subtracted from the fresh415 budgets. Nested profile spans are not
additive. The current joint implementation also starts its coefficient vector
at zero each call; useful previous solutions need a valid change of weighted
coordinates before they can become guesses.

The draft parallelizes group QR using existing idle worker observation scratch
and prepares disjoint pair couplings concurrently. Its three focused joint
analytic-oracle tests pass. Boundary, memory/allocation, public performance and
excluded-path checks remain pending; this is not production acceptance.

### Ordered bounded milestones

1. **Close the preparation experiment and use idle workers effectively.** Check
   deficient/empty groups, oversized local blocks, changing weights, failed-frame
   invalidation and allocation capacities. Run an early complete-command
   baseline/candidate/stock screen before broadening tests. Separately test
   parallel compact single-RHS FE products using existing worker banks, with
   ordered reductions and the existing observation-space curvature fallback.
   Preserve the fast small dense operator. This has a credible large-three-FE
   opportunity; it cannot by itself explain a 46 ms two-partition saving.

2. **Target the number and cost of complete changing-weight solves.** The main
   ambitious candidate is a multi-FE Poisson coefficient engine: conditional
   categorical updates and safeguarded group-local Newton updates for slope
   blocks, combined with finite-coefficient updates and objective-checked
   acceleration. Reuse immutable topology and bounded coefficient/work buffers.
   Extend the mathematical idea behind ADR 0127, not its one-FE analytic formula:
   multiple partitions are coupled and slopes have no general closed-form
   conditional solution. First compare a better slope initialization and ordinary
   nonlinear coefficient steps against the existing joint Newton route on actual
   PPML sequences. Count exponentials, full observation passes, outer steps,
   factor preparations and finalization work. Do not select an algorithm from
   cold fixed-weight kernel timings alone.

   Nonlinear steps propose model-space predictors; they must not masquerade as
   certified WLS outputs. A successor ADR must establish their acceptance and
   fallback boundary. Keep canonical initial rank, current objective and original
   FE/finite scores, strict current-weight projection, reconstruction and final
   rank/bread/Hessian/inference acceptance. Preserve numerical tolerances and
   separation. Use the existing joint solver for finishing or numerical refusal.
   Test mapping prior identified coefficients into the new weighted coordinates
   as a joint-solver starting guess, with a freshly formed current-weight initial
   residual. Prior coefficients may initialize work but never certify it.
   Start with two slope partitions, then test three-plus FE, categorical cases
   and low memory. Choose one coherent replacement rather than layering several
   competing permanent solvers.

3. **Make canonical construction and verification share necessary work.**
   Alongside the solver, map each check to its mathematical purpose, original
   inputs and sample/basis/weight generation. Fuse compatible reconstruction,
   residual-norm, moment and direct residual-Gram scans; write retained rows once
   where ownership permits. Keep independent acceptance grounded in original
   inputs and preserve cancellation-sensitive direct products. Geometry reuse
   within a weight frame already exists: remove measured duplication rather than
   proposing that cache again. Reuse a certified exact final weight state only
   through existing explicit generation authority. Never skip a check because a
   recurrence reports convergence. Measure the cost of mandatory verification
   separately after each solver improvement.

4. **Close categorical and narrow-fit gaps through shared lifecycle work.**
   Profile remaining native preparation, canonical work, inference and saved
   outputs in the complete command. Consolidate demonstrated duplicate design,
   topology, normalization and output passes, and use the nonlinear candidate
   only where its total cost wins. Preserve the one-call native architecture and
   independent transactional output validation. Existing interruption and native
   publication costs are too small to justify another tuning cycle. Keep wide,
   disconnected and four-plus-FE wins as controls; expand generated terms and
   cluster/output cases when they expose substantial costs.

5. **Freeze, validate, measure fresh cases and consolidate.** Each candidate
   needs focused independent explicit-design WLS and Poisson/Hessian/sandwich
   oracles, changing-frame/rank/separation/rollback checks, memory refusal and
   real warmed allocation checks where ownership changes. Use a small adaptive
   development screen, then freeze code before predeclaring fresh dense, sparse,
   weak, disconnected, unbalanced, multiple/deficient-slope, width, weight,
   T1/T4/T8, fast/low and inference/output cases. Include categorical PPML and
   OLS controls. Use five uncontended baseline/candidate/pinned-stock rotations
   for confirmation; record per-case medians, ranges, paired losses, failures
   and memory, with scientifically unresolved comparisons unranked. Commit
   accepted coherent changes, archive rejected experiments, remove superseded
   code, and update this opening with exact source/artifact identities.

Give each candidate one implementation and at most one evidence-led correction
before a public adopt/reject decision. Retain inexpensive reliable shared gains,
but do not mistake them for closing a family that needs 20--36%. Do not reopen
the rejected full dense factors, paired lanes or retained-product layouts by
tuning thresholds. If the ambitious nonlinear candidate fails, use its measured
solve/check/finalization breakdown to choose the next materially different
intervention. A target miss must name the remaining milliseconds and responsible
work, rather than claim that stronger science makes the gap inevitable.

No new validation seed is consumed by this planning update. Frozen 77/16/111
definitions, source-drift allocation failure, constrained-fit/CG failures and
deferred platform work remain unchanged. No push, release, SCC retry, stopped
campaign or qualification is authorized by this plan.

Move to **narrow categorical whole-command preparation/publication and native
setup**, using the existing source-bound phase diagnosis as the starting point.

it needs 16.4 ms (35%) total savings for the goal. Attribute the public Stata
boundary and native costs within the same command before changing ownership,
loading or repeated validation/normalization work. Then implement one coherent

The renewed plan targets **complete public PPML time <=0.90 times comparable
stock on designs with at least two FE**, with robust/clustered inference and
requested outputs charged. It is a per-family objective, not an aggregate win
rate. This is a planning update at `5dfe7cfb`; no new benchmark or implementation

Other fresh410 slope families already clear the target, including serial,
weakly connected, multiple-slope and disconnected examples. Preserve those
advantages. These sizes/seeds remain frozen observations, not tuning inputs.

1. **Close whole-command attribution before choosing the first edit.** Use
   existing development designs for narrow categorical, disconnected wider
   categorical, the two-partition slope thread-count loss, and large fast/low
   slopes. Instrument Stata preparation/validation/publication, native setup,
   initial rank, ordinary directions, strict finalization, inference and output
   within the same diagnostic command. Count observation passes, geometry builds,
   useful operator work, current-frame checks, worker submissions, main-thread
   interrupt exchanges and scratch traffic. Keep mutually exclusive phase totals
   separate from nested function spans. The existing current-frame diagnostic has
   about 32 ms inside the narrow plugin, including 7.1 ms canonical preparation
   and 6.2 ms ordinary joint solves; its uninstrumented command is 40 ms. Those
   separate runs cannot establish an 8 ms Stata-overhead estimate. They do show
   that boundary work alone is not an established explanation. Reuse the exact
   pinned reference's existing source analysis; instrument an isolated reference
   only to answer a remaining operation-count question. Deliver one cost ledger
   and a quantified savings hypothesis, then start implementation.

2. **Remove repeated work across the narrow public command.** Trace ownership
   from prepared immutable data through the current weighted frame and final
   publication. Consolidate demonstrated duplicate loading, normalization,
   reconstruction, metadata handling and repeated scans; include scheduling and
   interrupt-exchange cost if measured. Batch compatible work using the existing
   team and bounded storage. A publication receipt does not replace independent
   output validation, and cached input facts do not certify new weighted results.
   Preserve the main-thread SPI boundary and interruption/rollback behavior.
   Profile the complete candidate early: neither a faster kernel nor eliminating
   a one-millisecond phase can explain the required 16.4 ms saving alone. A simple
   reliable partial gain can be retained, but it does not close this family.

3. **Make canonical construction a larger computational intervention.** The
   two-categorical-FE fused product engine already exists. For three FE and slopes,
   investigate a common current-weight factorization serving all canonical RHSs,
   followed by bounded direct residual products, independently formed projection
   witnesses and one required retained-row write. The materially different solver
   candidate is rank-aware block elimination/factorization of the reduced system,
   with symbolic structure prepared once per sample and fresh numerical factors
   per weight frame. Compare complete setup, solve, certification, rank and
   inference costs against existing per-column Krylov work. Bound fill, factor
   work and all coexisting memory before allocation; large or ill-conditioned
   systems retain certified iterative solving. Local slope rank deficiency and
   component null spaces must follow the current policy. Do not revive the rejected
   retained-coefficient layouts, paired operators, lazy repeated row reconstruction
   or cancellation-sensitive Gram subtraction. Avoid adding another permanent
   solver unless full public gains justify it; integrate through the existing
   coefficient owner and remove superseded consumers after validation.

4. **Redesign verification as part of the computation, with explicit proofs.**
   Build a dependency table for every check: mathematical purpose, original inputs,
   valid sample/basis/weight generation and acceptance boundary. Share immutable
   geometry and compatible original-input scans; distinguish cheap recurrence
   diagnostics from independent acceptance. A new schedule needs a successor ADR,
   reduction-error argument and adversarial tests, not an assertion that two
   checks look redundant. Keep fresh current-weight projection, finite/FE scores,
   model space, rank/span, both inverse sides, objective, reconstruction and final
   Hessian acceptance. Measure required verification separately after solve costs
   fall. Do this alongside steps 2–3, rather than adding expensive full checks to
   every speculative solver update.

5. **Address the ordinary-direction/thread-count loss next if still dominant.**
   The current slope engine already solves finite and FE directions jointly;
   categorical PPML already has joint LSMR, warm starts and guarded preconditioning.
   First distinguish useful arithmetic from repeated products, synchronization,
   certificate scans and underused workers on identical frozen weighted frames.
   Compare at most two coherent organizations: retain the existing joint Krylov
   method with the new frame/product ownership, or use the reduced block solve
   from step 3 when measured factor work makes it cheaper. Prior-frame factors or
   solutions may be preconditioners/guesses only. Validate against current weights.
   Routing must follow structural work, conditioning and memory, never seeds,
   benchmark names or a guard chosen to hide the T8 loss.

6. **Expand evidence adaptively and consolidate production.** Once a candidate
   passes a small explicit WLS and Poisson/Hessian/sandwich oracle, run an early
   public baseline/candidate/stock rotation before expensive validation. Freeze
   promising code before declaring fresh cases: dense/sparse, disconnected/weak,
   unbalanced, multiple and deficient slopes, widths, weights, threads, fast/low,
   robust/cluster and saved outputs. Include focused categorical PPML and OLS
   controls, rank/separation/offset boundaries, changing-frame/rollback failures,
   and exact memory refusal. Remeasure older three-/four-plus-FE, wide/generated,
   inference and saved-output losses only as relevant; unresolved science remains
   unranked. Use at least five rotations for fresh confirmation, preserving every
   loss, tie, timeout and failed fit, paired distributions, source identities,
   tracked allocation peaks and process isolation. No competing work during
   headline timing. Commit accepted improvements with their evidence, delete
   rejected production code, and update this opening after each bounded milestone.

Each candidate gets one initial implementation and at most one materially
justified correction before an adopt/reject decision. Repeated 2–3% kernel or
whole-call gains with additional solver banks are not a reason to reopen the
closed experiments. Small broadly useful changes remain acceptable when cheap
in code and memory. If a family still misses 0.90, record the residual millisecond
budget and measured responsible phase; move to the next substantial opportunity
instead of indefinite threshold tuning. No universal parity promise follows.

## Multi-FE PPML implementation plan and current-frame diagnosis — 2026-09-24

The user requests an ambitious plan for **at least two FE partitions**, targeting
whole-public-command time <=0.90 times scientifically comparable pinned stock
fixest wherever reasonably achievable. The goal remains unfinished. This section
supersedes the previous suggestion to prioritize a standalone original-statistics
cache. It does not adopt a new algorithm or authorize weaker acceptance.

The [current-source diagnostic report](benchmarks/reports/development/ppml-current-frame-diagnosis-local-2026-09-24/README.md)
completes the pending screen at computational checkpoint **711802bf**. All 554
accepted artifact inputs match that checkpoint. Separate instrumentation captures
555 inputs. Thirty-two public-state checks and twelve stock comparisons pass;
all fits and isolation monitors pass. No estimator source changed. Its verified
archive preserves 1,991 logical receipts, 835 payloads and 6,812,930 bytes.
Development seed 202609347 remains a tuning seed; no fresh seed was consumed.

On the existing low-slope N61440/K10/T8 development case, uninstrumented fereg
is 243 [241,246] ms versus stock 231 [226,231], requiring another **35.1 ms**
for the target. Diagnostic initial/strict canonical solves total **92.37 ms**
inclusive; original-column statistics refresh is only **4.02 ms**. Fast canonical
work is 77.56 ms. These nested instrumented costs are prioritization evidence,
not additive phase accounting or headline speed claims.

### Ordered implementation milestones

1. **Generalize direct canonical products to absorbed slopes and then three-plus
   partitions.** Start with the current low/fast slope losses. The first candidate
   should fuse the existing coefficient-space projection's final original-input
   reconstruction with direct Gram/RHS, norms and independent FE moments, handing
   those products to canonical consumers and writing required retained rows once.
   Reuse current-weight group QR geometry across compatible RHS work under explicit
   frame ownership. Existing rank/QR/span fallbacks remain authoritative. Avoid
   cancellation-prone raw-minus-absorbed Gram subtraction. A second candidate is
   justified only if operation counts favor a different bounded block factor or
   preconditioner over the existing recurrence. Aim to halve the measured canonical
   work; this is an engineering target, not a forecast. Do not reintroduce the
   rejected lazy-row or frame-matvec organizations.
2. **Close narrow categorical whole-command losses.** The accepted fresh cases
   still need 25–33% total savings, and the new narrow development block needs 37%.
   Instrument Stata preparation/publication and native setup within matched public
   calls before attributing their gap. Then remove repeated metadata/topology,
   normalization, ownership conversion or output passes actually demonstrated by
   that trace. Reuse validated state through one transaction; retain main-thread
   SPI and all sample checks. Reduce fixed workspace/factor setup where it dominates
   small K. Existing conditional Poisson group optimization, deferred Schwarz and
   canonical-first finalization are already adopted, not new candidate ideas.
3. **Improve difficult ordinary solves only where they still dominate.** Compare
   identical frozen current-weight systems with stock operation counts. Investigate
   component/block elimination, effective block preconditioning and compatible
   coefficient warm starts. Separate topology from weighted geometry and current
   RHSs; warm starts never grant acceptance. Charge setup and fallback costs. Use
   mathematical size/connectivity/work and complete memory bounds for routing;
   never tune to case names, seeds or favorable timing outcomes. Retire superseded
   code after a replacement is established.
4. **Extend the winning mechanisms and close remaining output/memory costs.**
   Predeclare a compact fresh screen across dense, sparse, disconnected, weakly
   connected and unbalanced two/three/four-FE designs; numeric/generated widths;
   multiple slopes, changing weights and rank deficiency; T1/T4/T8; fast/low and
   refusal boundaries; robust/cluster inference and requested outputs. Expand
   around losses rather than run a Cartesian product. Investigate inference or
   publication as a primary target only if the refreshed whole-command profile
   supports it. Weighted-reference comparability must be adjudicated separately;
   ordinary fixest weights are not a frequency-weight inference oracle.

### Milestone acceptance and stopping rules

Each implementation milestone has one measured dominant-cost hypothesis and at
most two coherent candidate organizations before reassessment. Start with focused
independent WLS/Poisson/Hessian/sandwich oracles and adversarial frame/rank/memory
checks. Keep fresh residual, model-space, score, objective, reconstruction and
final-Hessian authority; verification fusion/rescheduling needs a successor ADR
and tests proving its scientific purpose. Preserve samples, weights, DoF,
separation, tolerances, interruption and failure atomicity.

Use three alternating baseline/candidate/stock rotations for an initial screen,
then predeclared fresh cases and seven rotations for promising candidates. Record
median/range, paired ratios and losses, iterations/operations, setup/solve/output
costs, tracked/modeled memory, timeouts and scientific failures. Marginal target
crossings need a separate predeclared confirmation block; do not repeat until a
win appears. Instrumented stock/native builds never supply headline timings.
No competing work may accompany those timings.

Protect accepted wins and excluded routes with focused categorical/slope OLS,
categorical/slope PPML, serial, low-memory, generated/weighted/cluster and saved-
output controls appropriate to each changed boundary. Keep the frozen 77/16/111
definitions intact. Retain small inexpensive shared gains when reliable, but do
not spend another milestone tuning a few milliseconds while larger gaps remain.
Commit each adopted implementation with durable ADR and source-bound evidence;
preserve rejected experiments and finish each milestone clean. No push, full
qualification, SCC retry or stopped campaign follows this plan.

The prior fresh source-bound block has four of ten cases below 0.90 stock and six
remaining losses: narrow fast/low 1.312/1.344, disconnected 1.244, unbalanced 1.205,
large low slopes 1.138 and two slope partitions 0.976. These ratios are case-bound,
not a global win rate. Existing allocation-inventory, constrained-fit, comparator
and deferred-platform failures remain open. Next action: fixed-frame prototype
of fused slope canonical products, with current cold/strict work as baseline.

### Adopted mechanism

The Stata adapter runs Rust-owned native PPML work in one scoped task on the
resolved team after loading. A stack exchange relays every existing interrupt
point to the Stata caller. The non-Send/non-Sync SPI callback stays there;
errors and either peer's panic close the exchange and join before publication.
T1 retains direct execution. The live scoped-job footprint enters embedding
admission before core preflight.

Prepared family mean/working rows use that installed team. Working weights,
responses and score residuals share a pass. The deviance uses the existing
cached log outcome. Objective row contributions use a bounded tile, followed
by the original observation-ordered compensated sums. Fresh final objective,
score, projection, model-space, rank, reconstruction, consecutive convergence,
separation and final-Hessian requirements are unchanged.

The first implementation repeatedly submitted individual family phases from the
calling thread. Its T4 audit caught one allocation with zero growth; external
Rayon submissions use a periodically allocated Crossbeam block queue. Scoped
execution passes the unchanged real 16-iteration T1/T4 audits and a separate
256-cycle allocation/callback test. No audit-only route or relaxed check exists.

### Adopted change and measured tradeoffs

P-by-W eliminated coefficient bank for output. When retained centers and full
post-certificate reconstruction exceed the existing allowance, it prepares the

pure coefficient recurrence supplies the original-input certificate and every

preparation, numerical or I/O failure. All scientific acceptance requirements
remain. Complete phase admission, work guards and outer budgets are unchanged;
affordable full banks stay preferred. No weighted authority crosses a call.

### Ambitious next plan: public PPML with at least two FE

1. **Account for the narrow/fast public gap before choosing the next engine.**
   N22560/K2 low needs 50→28.8 ms to beat stock by 10%, a 42.4% reduction.
   Its reported FE/finite/strict phases are 8.18/3.85/8.01 ms; inference is only
   0.30 ms. Fast K10 needs 67→52.2 ms, about 22%. Instrument an isolated native
   build and Stata wrapper to distinguish first-command loading, warm calls,
   preparation, ordinary directions, strict verification and publication.
   Match stock cold/warm work and keep diagnostic timings separate. Do not
   assign unaccounted public time to SPI or the wrapper without measurement.
2. **Prototype a fused current-weight two-FE joint solve.** Compare component
   Schur elimination of FE and finite coefficients with the existing ordinary
   coefficient/Krylov direction on identical frozen IRLS frames. Share immutable
   topology and current-frame factors across compatible RHS work, without
   materializing unnecessary N-by-K panels. Evaluate both dense and scratch
   consumers. All original-input projection, finite/rank/span, objective, score,
   reconstruction and final-Hessian requirements remain. Changing weights only
   permit prior solutions as guesses. Any cold-routing extension must follow
   measured computational work, not another inflation of the closed work hint.
3. **Keep the next experiment bounded and consequential.** Predeclare a small
   current-baseline set, then fresh connected/disconnected/unbalanced cases at
   narrow/moderate widths and larger N, T1/T4/T8, plus slope/three-FE/OLS controls.
   Aim for a coherent 20–40% public improvement on losing two-FE families. Stop a
   candidate when its measured phase ceiling cannot deliver a material gain;
   do not keep tuning to favorable seeds. Commit accepted changes and losses.
4. **Return to wide memory limits as the second subsystem.** Actual topology
   gives disconnected P9200/Q920 a minimum solve bank of 8,968,720 bytes versus
   8,832,000 allowed: bounded RHS reductions are the concrete next mechanism.
   K140 needs 4,533,632 bytes for full coefficient reconstruction versus
   3,456,000 allowed: tile that output stage without a full P-by-W bank. These
   are structural calculations corroborated by unchanged runtime peaks/phases,
   not instrumented route counters. Avoid budget increases or shape-specific
   thresholds. Broaden only after an independently validated public gain.

Preserve the 77/16/111 definitions and all frozen seeds. Keep one-FE work outside
the goal except focused regression controls. Do not retry SCC or restart stopped
reference/empirical campaigns. The target is broad practical speed; these results
do not establish a universal 10% advantage.

### What changed and what the experiment proves

Both candidates eliminate the larger categorical partition, prepare a grounded,
scaled current-weight Schur factor and solve all compatible RHSs against it.
Algebraic products subtract `U'U` from a centered Gram; the **selected fused
candidate instead reconstructs each row once in group-disjoint work**, forming
the direct full Gram/RHS, within norms and independent original-design FE scores
together. It avoids nearly equal Gram subtraction and does not retain an N-by-K
result panel merely to compute products. The existing joint Hessian is only
partially absorbed and cannot substitute for these final products.

Eight declared frames use four existing lifecycle designs plus deterministic
positive weight perturbations; no fresh validation seed was consumed. At
T1/T4/T8, seven alternating B/A/C rotations compare the accepted low-memory
response/control-panel/scratch-moment pipeline with both candidates. These are
**fixed weighted-linear product calls**, excluding canonical rank/QR, final
inference, requested outputs and public transactions. Required later row
materialization must still be charged in the public integration.

Representative final-block medians (milliseconds):

| Frame | Accepted panels | Fused products | Candidate setup | Preparation-charged C/B |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Wide N16320/K32/T8 | 19.177 | 2.267 | 0.352 | 0.136 |
| Unbalanced N16320/K12/T4 | 7.270 | 1.204 | 0.997 | 0.299 |
| Narrow N12000/K3/T1 | 3.982 | 0.503 | 0.235 | 0.182 |
| Disconnected N20160/K12/T4 | 8.257 | 2.786 | 5.255 | 0.961 |

All 168 warm pairs improve for each final candidate. Preparation-charged ratios
are estimates from separately observed setup, not repeated cold-call timings.
Disconnected T4 is a weak result: its two fused estimates are 0.961/0.976 and
the preceding algebraic-only block loses at 1.043/1.019 after setup. Dense-factor
assembly/factorization work therefore needs structural admission. Fused products
are sometimes slower than algebraic products, but retain the large baseline
gains while removing that subtraction's extra numerical proof burden. Select
only the fused candidate for production, not overlapping alternatives.

All **72 independent projection/Gram configurations** (1,134 column checks),
**72 separate explicit-FE/QR finite coefficient/inverse configurations**, and
**three final-source Rust boundary tests** pass. Maximum fused projection error
is 1.169e-14, original-design score 3.322e-16, Gram error 1.554e-14 and inverse
error 1.621e-14. Boundaries cover near-FE-collinearity, changing weights, threads,
disconnected component mass ratios of 160 orders, column scales spanning 140
orders and invalid inputs. This does not replace public Poisson/Hessian,
rank/omission, memory or transactional validation.

Illustrative explicit payload estimates are 1,373,408 bytes wide T8 and 259,520
unbalanced T4; these exclude source/allocator/export overhead and are not tracked
public peaks or production admission. Prototype allocations are ordinary vectors.
No public, stock, licensed-Stata, OLS timing, memory-cap or platform campaign was
run here. Existing public ratios and unresolved disconnected stock science remain
those in the preceding closeout below.

## Historical: PPML frame-operator design selected — 2026-09-24

The active goal remains **whole-public PPML <=0.90 times comparable pinned stock
fixest wherever reasonably achievable with at least two FE partitions**. It is
unfinished. Production computation remains **`2c34503d`**, artifact
**`jointpanels2`**, plugin SHA-256
`4d4c669d6716583b14be437e2732133d61f733840b610414429d8df5614168b1`.
Neither prototype below is admitted or routed in production. The only source
change at this checkpoint repairs test-only checkpoint accounting.

The [completed lifecycle/design-selection report](benchmarks/reports/development/ppml-frame-operator-local-2026-09-24/README.md)
captures isolated diagnostic `frameledger1`, both frozen operator prototypes,
all distributions, independent oracles and failed builds. Its **2,123 logical
receipts** were verified and restored; archive SHA-256
`edbd169f91aa568a6e8c61595741bf2072315c8ef6c00bf34682df85becba15b`.
All builds, diagnostic fits, probes, tests and archive/restore processes are
terminal. No stock timing, fresh seed campaign or new whole-public speedup claim
belongs to this milestone.

### What the experiment established

- All **14 diagnostic public fits and independent public-state checks pass**.
  Wide low two-FE makes **11 canonical Schur calls across only two weight
  frames**, with 78 operator applications and 15,014,400 observation-by-RHS
  visits. Its measured operator work takes about 12.5 ms, initialization 3.9–5.0,
  reconstruction 2.0–2.7 and final certificates 8.5–8.7. These are instrumented
  diagnostic phases; nested certificate spans must not be added twice.
- Reusable edge operators improve 22/33 warm configurations and lose 11;
  only nine improve with all setup charged to one call. **Reject broad
  edge-only adoption.** Wide and narrow designs have no repeated pairs, so
  edge compression is not their missing advantage.
- A **frame-owned reduced matrix inside the existing PCG recurrence** improves
  all 24 small-system warm medians by **29–59%**. All nine larger disconnected
  medians lose **6–142%**. Only eight configurations improve after charging full
  setup to one call. Wide width10/T8 is 4.559→2.396 ms warm with 1.283 ms setup;
  unbalanced width10/T4 is 3.487→1.920 with 2.291 ms setup. This supports reuse
  across compatible calls, with structural work/memory admission, not universal
  dense routing or a claim that preparation is free.
- **582 explicit-design WLS oracle checks per prototype pass**. These are
  identical frozen final weights/RHSs at tolerance 1e-12, seven alternating
  pairs per configuration. Changing-weight ownership, extreme-weight safety
  and whole-public Poisson/Hessian integration still need validation.
- The prior actual2/expected3 checkpoint test failure is resolved as a
  **test-accounting bug**: a rank-zero external fused Newton witness contributes
  a reported checkpoint without refreshing the canonical session. A test-only
  counter records that successful witness separately. All **three focused
  regressions pass**. Production reporting and scientific behavior are unchanged.

### Implementation plan and measurable exit conditions

1. **Integrate one frame-owned reduced operator.** Keep immutable FE topology
   and prepare the current-weight reduced matrix once for compatible control
   tiles, response and checkpoint consumers. Response-only changes may reuse
   it; sample/topology/weight changes and failed construction invalidate it.
   Use exact symmetric construction, existing component scaling, fallible
   fixed capacities and complete live-memory admission. Compare q² operator
   work with two observation passes and include assembly degree costs in the
   structural decision. The larger disconnected system must retain the current
   operator when preparation or application is unfavorable. Do not add another
   edge-only solver layer or borrow OLS cache authority. Preserve original-input
   reconstruction and independent certificates. First gate: independent WLS,
   changing/extreme weights, weak/disconnected graphs, rank-zero, interruption,
   refusal and generation tests; then an early whole-public baseline/candidate/
   stock screen. Kernel gains alone do not justify adoption.
2. **Attack the remaining full-command passes.** The operator attribution
   cannot by itself supply the wide/unbalanced 34–40% reductions still needed.
   After measuring integration, address the dominant remaining initial/final
   canonical construction, reconstruction and checking work. Compare one
   coherent alternative: raw weighted moments plus certified FE coefficient
   products, retaining canonical rank/QR/span authority and cancellation bounds.
   Materialize rows for consumers that require them. A replacement verification
   schedule needs an explicit mathematical argument, successor ADR and
   adversarial independent tests; no tolerance or acceptance condition changes.
   Do not repeat ADR0164's rejected lazy row-view or per-call dense checkpoint.
3. **Remove common overhead to carry near-parity families below 0.90 stock.**
   Remeasure narrow, disconnected, three-FE and slope controls after the larger
   changes. Consolidate loading, original-input scans, inference and requested
   outputs where phase evidence supports it. Target shared savings rather than
   seed-specific guards or prolonged tuning for a 1-ms remainder. Keep the
   accepted slope engine and categorical OLS gains protected.
4. **Expand by topology and work, not a large Cartesian campaign.** Predeclare
   fresh cases for larger N, four-plus FE, multiple slope partitions, wider and
   generated controls, imbalance, weak/disconnected topology, rank deficiency,
   changing/extreme weights, T1/T4/T8, low budgets and robust/cluster/full outputs.
   Each accepted mechanism gets independent WLS/Poisson/Hessian/weight checks,
   five uncontended baseline/candidate/pinned-stock rotations on fresh cases,
   distributions including losses and failures, complete memory accounting and
   a coherent local commit. Protect one-FE PPML and categorical/slope OLS with
   focused excluded-path controls. Scientifically unresolved comparisons stay
   unranked; 0.90 is assessed per comparable whole-command case.

   the baseline checkpoint-count discrepancy as a separate bounded test-policy
   audit without changing scientific behavior to satisfy a count assertion.
2. **Give compatible projections one explicit frame owner.** Current source
   recomputes weighted group totals in `absorb_two_fe_pcg_reusing`; compiled
   weighted-neighbor reuse is guarded to OLS and PPML uses observation operators.
   This is a source-supported hypothesis, not measured attribution. If repeated
   work is substantial, retain immutable topology and prepare weighted geometry
   once per valid frame for compatible control tiles, response and checkpoint
   consumers. Separate their RHS/convergence state. Reuse prior coefficients as
   guesses only. Replace the call-owned organization where justified; do not

   Require generation invalidation, complete live-memory admission, independent

3. **Eliminate duplicated canonical products/passes if they remain dominant.**
   Compare at most one materially different second organization: raw weighted
   moments plus certified FE coefficients, with cancellation bounds and canonical
   rank/QR/span authority, materializing rows only for consumers that need them.
   This algebraic design is unimplemented; the rejected lazy-row view did not
   test it. Shared verification calculations may change only with an explicit
   invariant/error-bound argument, successor ADR and adversarial tests. Fresh
   residual, score, objective, reconstruction and final-Hessian acceptance remain.
   Stop a candidate after a bounded public screen if its gain is small,
   inconsistent or bought with disproportionate memory/complexity.
4. **Close shared overhead and near-parity losses after the large redesign.**
   Current disconnected and narrow anchors need 15.7 and 7.2 ms (18.5%/13.3%)

5. **Broaden successful mechanisms with fresh, predeclared tests.** Include

   extreme weights, rank deficiency, T1/T4/T8, low budgets and optional refusal.

### Ambitious implementation plan, in priority order

1. **Remove whole-model access cliffs and repeated original-control passes.**
   Verify actual binding decisions with isolated counters: `NumericOlsColumns`
   currently rejects the complete model above 64 columns or when any recipe is
   generated. A public K64 model may include an intercept and cross that limit;
   this is a source lead, not yet measured attribution. Compare per-column
   binding with bounded block binding so numeric columns stay direct in wide
   and mixed models. Preserve fallible generated access and bounded memory.

   Carry this organization through stable norms, products, reconstruction and
   original-input score scans. Share statistics only within a valid current
   frame; avoid another full observation matrix or a stack array sized by the
   complete design. Count recipe dispatches, bytes read and complete passes.
   Target a material whole-fit reduction on wide models, including K63/64/65
   boundaries and mixed generated/numeric controls. A threshold increase alone
   is not the intended redesign. This cannot by itself be presumed to close the
   40–51% remaining dense losses.

2. **Make accepted-frame finalization one coherent computation.** Trace exact
   duplicated geometry, projection, normalized products and reconstruction
   across strict validation, canonical rank, bread/Hessian and inference. Give
   compatible current-frame products one explicit owner keyed by sample,
   topology, generated basis, raw weights and generation; invalidate on every
   dependency change. Borrow the established final design and products rather
   than recreate them. Use independent RHS stopping and compatible response/
   control fusion where projection work remains dominant.

   Separate cheap speculative diagnostics from independent accepted-result
   checks. Change check scheduling only with a successor ADR demonstrating the
   preserved invariant and focused failure-injection tests. Current-weight
   original-input projection/model-space/score, objective, rank and final-Hessian
   acceptance remain mandatory. Neither old-frame factors nor ordinary Newton
   products acquire rank/covariance authority. Do not revive the rejected
   all-coefficient canonical route by simply removing its guard.

3. **Replace the fast categorical bottleneck and unify successful routes.**
   The current fast categorical case needs about a **51%** reduction to reach
   its 56.7-ms target. Compare its full LSMR organization with the adopted
   coefficient/joint route on identical frozen weight frames, measuring setup,
   products, observation passes, reconstruction and acceptance. If joint
   directions win, introduce a shared ordinary engine with explicit memory
   admission and one certified fallback; retire the displaced duplication.
   Otherwise identify the measured dominant fast cost and redesign that stage.
   Do not force a solver based on the name of a benchmark or reinterpret the
   low-mode timings as proof that a fast-mode substitution will win.

   Carry the winning dataflow through categorical and multiple-slope designs,
   fast and low storage, while protecting weak/disconnected winners. Recheck
   the historical large slopes and selected higher-FE cases on the resulting
   source. Apply common improvements to OLS only with independent projection,
   inference, admission and timing controls. The adopted coefficient-space
   slope engine is the starting point, not a proposal for a new experiment.

4. **Close one-FE and public-output costs.** Use the already profiled one-FE
   concentrated Poisson owner; identify what still costs 40 ms against stock's
   26-ms control and a 23.4-ms target. Measure loading/control-plane, concentrated
   solve, final inference and publication independently. Share accepted means,
   bounded score blocks and certified products where valid. Include small fits,
   robust/clustered inference, generated terms and requested saved effects.
   Investigate the large one-FE scientific discrepancy independently before
   ranking it. A different estimand, separation sample or omitted output cannot
   count as a speedup. Keep main-thread SPI, one substantive call and atomic
   publication; do not offload native computation into ado/Mata.

5. **Demand per-case success and stop low-value loops.** For each milestone,
   first establish its avoidable-cost ceiling. Test at most two coherent
   designs, then reassess rather than fitting more thresholds. Seek compound
   gains large enough to halve the remaining dense runtimes where the measured
   work supports that ambition. Retain smaller broad, inexpensive improvements,
   but do not treat them as completion of the target.

   Freeze candidates before predeclaring 4–6 fresh cases and excluded-path
   controls. Cover imbalance, weak connectivity, disconnection, widths, multiple
   slopes, rank deficiency, changing/dynamic-range weights, T1/T4/T8, memory
   modes and requested outputs across these bounded milestones. Require
   independent WLS and Poisson/Hessian/sandwich oracles, then alternating
   baseline/candidate/pinned-stock rotations with at least five fresh
   confirmations. No builds, profiling, archiving or competing fits beside
   headline clocks. Report distributions, every paired loss, failures, memory
   costs and exact source/artifact identities. Cases with scientific
   discrepancies stay unranked. Repeatable <=0.90 whole-command ratios are the
   target; aggregate win rates and inner-kernel wins are insufficient.

Commit accepted changes and rejected evidence at each boundary. Where a target

### Adopted solver and scientific evidence

A PPML-specific reusable two-FE owner enters Schur PCG after its initial
certificate, without four mandatory symmetric MAP pilots. Disconnected blocks
and their Jacobi diagonals are scaled by the largest current right-group mass
within each component. Immutable roots are prepared per owner; masses/scales
refresh under every weight frame. Original-weight reconstruction and independent
acceptance remain, as do canonical rank, score, objective, strict-profile,
final-Hessian and publication requirements. Ordinary OLS construction/admission,
checkpoint-LSMR policy and one-/three-FE/slope algorithms retain their behavior.

Direct entry alone failed an existing six-step dynamic-range PPML boundary.
A finishing sweep and centered-RHS probe also failed. Component balancing repairs
that boundary without tolerance changes. A shared-constructor prototype was
replaced by the PPML-specific constructor to protect exact OLS memory admission.

### Ambitious implementation plan, in priority order

1. **Remove repeated finite-product construction from ordinary IRLS.** Close
   direct-Schur/pilot tuning now. The final wide diagnostic attributes 58.94 ms
   to six joint directions: 29.69 ms finite tiles, 5.69 ms norms and 11.14 ms
   reconstruction, with exclusive recurrence below 1 ms. Source confirms that
   `JointFiniteWorkspace::solve_streamed` rebuilds all K-by-K Hessian and FE/control
   cross-products under every frame. Its current dense operator makes recurrence
   cheap but charges O(NK²) preparation repeatedly.

   Compare two coherent candidates on identical frozen frames: (a) an exact
   current-weight matrix-free joint operator, with compatible previous factors
   used only as preconditioners and previous solutions only as initial guesses;
   (b) blocked/batched current-weight products with admitted bounded scratch and
   vectorized independent accumulators. Candidate (a) must explicitly transport
   coordinates/scales, preserve symmetric positive preconditioning and invalidate
   reuse on sample/topology/basis changes. Current-weight geometry and acceptance
   remain fresh. Measure total preparation plus operator passes, not iteration
   count alone. Use operation/memory cost and conditioning to select a policy;
   do not key it to benchmark names or seeds. Retire a superseded ordinary path
   after evidence establishes replacement; retain one certified fallback.

   Aim for a substantial whole-fit reduction, around 25–40% on the dense/wide
   targets, rather than a few percent in the recurrence. This is an experiment
   target, not a promised result or enough by itself to reach 77.4 ms.

2. **Unify current-frame projection and canonical products.** The same wide
   diagnostic still spends 28.13 ms in canonical projection and 17.22 ms in rank
   work; the narrower case spends 15.88 and 10.61 ms. Track exact duplicated group
   masses/factors, normalization, RHS passes and retained products across tiles,
   strict candidates and final inference. Introduce one explicit owner for
   compatible current-frame geometry/products, keyed to sample, design, basis,
   raw weights and generation. Separate immutable topology from weighted state.
   Share compatible RHS work and stop columns independently. Reconstruct each
   accepted state once and share established products with downstream consumers.

   Redesign intermediate diagnostics where they duplicate a separately proven
   invariant; retain independent original-input projection/model-space/score,
   objective and final-Hessian acceptance. Document any changed check schedule
   in a successor ADR with failure-injection tests. Prior-frame preconditioners
   must never become current rank or covariance authority. The prior rejected
   all-coefficient canonical route is not adopted by removing its guard.

3. **Carry the best mechanism through fast, low and slope PPML.** Use the existing
   coefficient-space slope/joint engine as the starting point; do not propose it
   as new work. Rebaseline the original two-slope and unbalanced three-FE designs
   on the adopted source, including multiple slopes and larger K. Explain why
   fast execution still loses on the current categorical control, then replace
   duplicated dense/streamed organization when one shared implementation is
   better. Protect weak/disconnected cases already winning. Bring the current
   slope control from 139 toward 104.4 ms and the three-FE control below 217.8 ms;
   do not spend a long separate cycle on the last 3% of one case while dense
   categorical cases require 50–61% reductions. Generalize to OLS only when a
   focused independent projection oracle, memory admission and timing controls
   support it.

4. **Close one-FE, inference and public-command overhead.** Reuse the earlier
   source-bound inventory to choose a small current-source one-FE screen. Do not
   restart broad campaigns. Profile robust/cluster score products, final means,
   saved effects, loading, metadata parsing and publication separately from IRLS.
   Apply accepted-frame ownership, bounded batching and fewer complete row passes
   where evidence supports them. Include generated/factor controls and small
   fits. Improve the Stata control-plane portion when it is measured as dominant,
   preserving main-thread SPI, one substantive native call and atomic publication.

5. **Finish with per-case evidence, not an aggregate win rate.** After a candidate
   freezes, predeclare a new validation seed and 4–6 cases around the affected
   family plus excluded-path controls. Include imbalance, weak connectivity,
   disconnection, wide controls, multiple slopes, changing/dynamic-range weights,
   rank deficiency, T1/T4/T8, low/fast execution and requested robust/cluster/saved
   outputs across the bounded milestones. Use independent explicit-design WLS
   and Poisson/Hessian/sandwich oracles. Keep comparator sample/separation/
   objective discrepancies unranked and preserve failures and timeouts.

   Use alternating baseline/candidate/pinned-stock rotations, typically three
   for development and at least five fresh confirmations. No builds/profiling/
   archiving or competing fits beside headline clocks. Report all paired losses,
   distributions, operation counts, memory costs and exact artifacts. A 10% claim
   needs <=0.90 per comparable case and repeatable fresh evidence; a tiny or noisy
   timing does not establish it. Do not loosen accuracy or omit requested outputs.
   Leave the frozen 77/16/111 definitions intact. SCC and physical-memory checks
   remain deferred until access is renewed, without authentication retries.

Each milestone gets at most two materially different candidate designs before
reassessing its measured savings ceiling. Retain reliable smaller gains when
broad and inexpensive, but do not substitute them for closing the large gaps.
Commit accepted implementations and rejected evidence, then move to the next
largest avoidable cost. If a case remains above target, record the residual
phase budget and tested alternatives that explain the limit. Neither current
certification costs nor fixest parity are assumed to be unavoidable ceilings.

Static allocation source drift, weighted constrained-fit failures, nonretaining
CG instability, historical stock-mean discrepancies and the 1e6-FE-shift failure
retain their scope. No push, release, stopped-campaign restart or SCC retry.

### Mechanism and validation

Reusable two-FE categorical initial checks and MAP pilots temporarily lend idle
PCG group banks to existing parallel kernels. The loan requires multiple workers,
at least 16384 row-by-RHS entries, empty ordinary group banks and an admitted
two-FE owner. A scoped destructor restores ownership before recurrence, error or
unwind. PCG reconstructs its current-weight state; no numerical authority crosses
weight frames. No new bank, memory formula, solver, tolerance, check schedule,
rank/DoF, sample, separation or publication policy is added. One-shot OLS, slopes
and three-FE algorithms remain unchanged.

**156 distinct final-source Rust tests**, production ABI/panic checks and

disconnection, unequal changing component masses, a zero RHS, exact serial/
parallel results and poisoned-bank error/panic restoration. A local public
N4800/K8/pool4 explicit Poisson/Hessian/sandwich oracle covers unit/FW/PW,
robust/cluster and T1/T4. Allocation, multipartition slopes, separation and
transaction fixtures also pass. The allocation window covers ordinary joint
iterations, not canonical pilots; the Rust test covers loan capacity/ownership.

All **189 headline applications**, **177 public-state checks**, **57 exact native
export pairs**, **63 baseline/stock** and **51 direct candidate/stock pairs**
pass. No scientific exclusions, application failures, timeouts or detected
contention. Eight diagnostic applications are separate. All 51 PPML pairs retain

### Implementation plan, in priority order

1. **Make low multi-FE canonical construction competitive.** Start with identical
   frozen accepted weights/RHS/controls for low three-FE and multipartition
   slopes. Attribute initialization, current-weight geometry, individual RHS
   convergence, scratch traversal, reconstruction and final checks separately.
   The current low three-FE strict/final marginal is **171.662 ms** versus
   **0.615 ms inference**; the joint strict witness already works. Target the
   initial/final canonical dataflow, not another ordinary-direction solver.
   First candidate: let the existing current-frame coefficient/geometry owner
   stream canonical corrections in bounded RHS tiles, stop each RHS independently,
   and avoid repeated scratch read/normalize/write passes. Form compatible finite
   products during construction where this preserves an independent later check.
   Retain original-input reconstruction, local relative projection accuracy,
   canonical rank/QR fallback, both inverse sides and final q*mu authority.
   Do not replay ADR 0136's rejected all-coefficient categorical route without a
   materially new local-scaling/error-control design. If streaming cannot remove
   the dominant cost, compare one genuinely different canonical coefficient
   formulation, using the same frozen-frame oracle and operation ledger. The
   public goals are <=211 ms for this dense low cell and <=108 ms for both slope
   modes, requiring about 39%, 28% and 14% reductions respectively.

2. **Redesign narrow one-FE end to end.** The 97 -> 46.8-ms target requires removing
   roughly half the public command. Freeze a narrow N/K ladder, including small
   fits, and compare stock setup, solve, inference and outputs with equivalent
   requested work. Trace Stata syntax/metadata, SPI loading, sample/topology,
   canonical initialization/finalization, objective/score passes and publication.
   Prototype one sample-generation owner for immutable recipes/membership and
   one explicitly invalidated current-weight product owner where duplicate work
   is measured. Investigate fused native passes and direct grouped canonical
   products; retain independent final projection/rank/Hessian and original-input
   score checks. For one-FE initialization, evaluate a cheaper scientifically
   equivalent construction rather than presuming a complete generic transaction
   is necessary twice. Avoid unsafe subtraction of large nearly equal Grams.
   Keep Stata as the control plane, main-thread SPI and receipt-last atomicity.
   If language/control-plane overhead dominates small fits, address it directly
   through shared native metadata and fewer duplicated traversals, not work moved
   outside the reported timer. Compare fast versus implicit storage by actual
   cost/admission evidence; the previously rejected narrow fast implicit route
   is not automatically revived.

3. **Remove wide-column and verification bottlenecks.** Extend numeric binding
   for PPML original-input scores through bounded column blocks instead of the
   >64-column serial generic fallback; preserve each column's compensated row
   order and independent score authority. Reorganize the two reported inverse
   checks as bounded contiguous kernels, retaining their actual residual bounds.
   Profile robust/cluster score reductions and output validation separately.
   K80 baseline diagnostic costs include about 14 ms outer scores, 10 ms reported
   inverse/intercept checks, 24–25 ms inference and 10 ms publication metadata;
   not all are column-evaluation costs. Do not repeat the completed covariance
   eigensystem/pivot tuning. The K80/T8 goal needs another **55.5 ms**, so evaluate
   the combined whole-command budget, not a fast microbenchmark alone. Carry
   shared kernels into OLS only with its focused scientific/performance controls.
   K48/K24's 1–2-ms residual gaps may close incidentally; no dedicated long cycle.

4. **Expand coverage adaptively and choose routes from costs.** Current-source
   evidence is strongest for the listed one-FE widths and dense/slope controls.
   Earlier disconnected/weak/sparse/unbalanced, higher-dimensional, multi-slope,
   generated/factor, clustered/weighted and saved-output results stay attached
   to their historical artifacts until remeasured. Comparator discrepancies stay
   unranked; untested combinations remain explicitly untested. For each changed
   boundary, predeclare a small fresh panel spanning those relevant axes, T1/T4/T8,
   widths on both sides of existing representation boundaries, changing/extreme
   weights and rank deficiency. Start around the measured problem; extend only
   when evidence exposes a route boundary. Automatic routing may use stable
   mathematical dimensions, topology, measured work estimates and admitted
   memory, never benchmark names/seeds. Compare alternatives on identical frozen
   frames before integrating a route and retire superseded production machinery.

5. **Close each family with durable evidence and then move on.** Each milestone
   gets a current-source baseline, phase/operation ledger, at most two materially
   different candidates, independent explicit-design WLS/Poisson/Hessian checks,
   alternating baseline/candidate/stock rotations, fresh confirmation and focused
   excluded PPML/OLS controls. Use at least five rotations where margins matter;
   assess variability as well as medians, and report the worst losses and failures.
   A claimed 10% lead needs <=0.90 per comparable case plus fresh confirmation;
   a three-rotation control is not a family-wide claim. Retain smaller coherent,
   reliable improvements when cheap, but do not stop the larger task there.
   Commit accepted changes/ADRs and immutable receipts; rejected candidates retain
   evidence and a reason. If a target remains missed, supply the remaining phase
   budget and a concrete next mechanism or measured limiting cost. No generic
   assertion that certification makes parity impossible.

### Adopted mechanism and limits

Low one-intercept-FE publication PPML optionally owns fresh weighted group centers
and immutable shared prepared inputs through final inference. Canonical moments,
rank/QR fallback and inference stream original-minus-center rows. There is no
retained projected scratch matrix on this admitted route. Genuine interaction
partitions and generated columns use the same mechanism. Every refresh revokes
old authority, recomputes current-weight statistics and independently replays
residual group moments. All rank, score, objective, reconstruction, Hessian,
weight, separation and publication requirements remain unchanged.

The dual-mode prototype `groupcanon2` increased narrow fast finite-moment cost;
fast adoption is rejected. Production fast retains its contiguous dense design.
This is an execution-mode decision, not a benchmark/seed/shape threshold. Group
state, bindings, workers and shared-owner allocation are charged before use;
optional refusal keeps the certified scratch route. G-by-K geometry can be large
when G approaches N. The existing conservative scratch/projection allowance is
not credited back, so modeled peak can rise despite a smaller tracked peak.

**422 distinct Rust tests**, production-plugin ABI/panic containment and **14
licensed runs of 11 fixtures** pass on the final source. Independent closed-form
projection/WLS and full-dummy Poisson/Hessian/sandwich checks include changing and
extreme weights, rank deficiency, zero controls, generated terms, interactions,
FW/PW, offsets and robust/clustered inference. Three fixed-process allocation
audits retain zero events/growth and warm/cold equivalence. A one-byte optional
budget refusal changes actual scratch 0 -> 65,536 bytes and still passes its
independent Poisson oracle.

The adopted source has **160 passing applications**, 144 passing PPML states,
48 native PPML pairs, 48 baseline/stock and 48 additional direct stock checks.
Eight excluded PPML and eight OLS pairs have exact scientific exports. The report
separates prototype evidence and nine prototype-only small Python oracles. Two
previous blocks stopped on unrelated Stata overlaps; their 54 attempts and two
flagged overlaps are preserved and excluded from the clean timing tables.
